steps: Pressure cook the potato, cauliflower, carrot and peas with about 100 ml water a person, 5 to 6 whistles, until very soft. Mash them.
Melt half the butter in a wide pan on medium and fry most of the onion for 3 to 4 minutes, until soft.
Add the crushed ginger, garlic and green chilli and fry for a minute, until fragrant.
Add the capsicum for 2 to 3 minutes, then the tomato and salt, and cook 6 to 7 minutes until mushy.
Stir in the turmeric, chilli powder and most of the pav bhaji masala and fry for 2 minutes, until the raw smell goes.
Add the mashed vegetables with their cooking water, mash again and simmer on low for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Slit the pav and toast it on low to medium heat in a little butter with a pinch of pav bhaji masala, a minute or two a side.
Top the bhaji with a knob of butter and the coriander, and serve with the pav, the rest of the onion raw and lemon wedges.
note: Butter is 20 g a plate across cooking, toasting and topping, a little less than the street-style sources. Pav is listed as an ingredient at two rolls a plate because it has to be bought fresh on the day.
